name: APT29 Stage 1 - Domain Trust and Local Account Discovery (T1482 / T1087.001)
blast_radius: Runs nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts and net user through cmd.exe with output redirected into a run-tagged temp directory. Read-only. APT29 maps trusts with nltest before lateral movement. The temp directory is removed and removal is verified.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 1: cmd.exe, nltest.exe and net.exe with the run-tagged output path
Security EID 4688: process creation with command line, if command-line auditing is enabled
detection: EDR: nltest.exe domain trust enumeration from a script host (Sigma proc_creation_win_nltest_recon)
SIEM: nltest.exe and net.exe user in one command line, the APT29 recon pattern

name: APT29 Stage 2a - Encoded PowerShell Payload Download from a Loopback Server (T1105 / T1059.001)
blast_radius: Starts a loopback-only HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1, launches an encoded PowerShell child that downloads a short text payload and saves it to a run-tagged temp file. The payload is never executed. No traffic leaves the host. The listener is stopped and the file removed.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 1: powershell.exe -EncodedCommand with the run-tagged working directory
PowerShell EID 4104: decoded download command in script block logging
Sysmon EID 3: connection to 127.0.0.1 on the listener port
detection: EDR: encoded PowerShell with a web download (Sigma proc_creation_win_powershell_encoded_cmd)
AMSI/ScriptBlock: DownloadString in a decoded command

name: APT29 Stage 2b - Layered Encoded PowerShell Executed Locally (T1059.001 / T1027 / T1140)
blast_radius: Launches PowerShell with a two-layer encoded command that decodes and runs a benign command writing one marker file in a run-tagged temp directory. No network use. The directory is removed and removal is verified.
telemetry: PowerShell EID 4104: both decoded layers in script block logging
Security EID 4688: child powershell.exe with the encoded argument
detection: EDR: nested encoded PowerShell and Invoke-Expression of decoded content

name: APT29 Stage 3 - HKCU Run Key Persistence Write, Read-back and Removal (T1547.001)
blast_radius: Writes one run-tagged value under HKCU Software Microsoft Windows CurrentVersion Run that echoes a marker, reads it back and deletes it, then verifies the value is gone. User-level only; the value is never executed by a logon.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 13 and 14: registry value set and deleted under the Run key
Security EID 4657: registry value modified, if object-access auditing is enabled
detection: EDR: new HKCU Run value written by a script host (Sigma registry_set_persistence_run_key)
SIEM: Run value created and deleted within seconds
cleanup:
Get-ChildItem -Path $env:TEMP -Filter 'bas_a29_*' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$k = 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'; (Get-Item -Path $k -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Property | Where-Object { $_ -like 'bas_a29_*' } | ForEach-Object { Remove-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name $_ -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }

name: APT29 Stage 4 - Scheduled Task Created, Run Once, Queried and Deleted (T1053.005)
blast_radius: Creates a one-time scheduled task with a run-tagged name whose action writes a marker file, runs it once, then deletes it and verifies deletion with a query. Current user only, no elevation, no trigger that fires later.
telemetry: Security EID 4698 and 4699: task created and deleted, if object-access auditing is enabled
Task Scheduler EID 106 and 200: task registered and action started
Sysmon EID 1: schtasks.exe with the run-tagged task name
detection: EDR: schtasks.exe /create from a script host (Sigma proc_creation_win_schtasks_persistence)
SIEM: new scheduled task outside a change window
cleanup:
Get-ChildItem -Path $env:TEMP -Filter 'bas_a29_*' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'bas_a29_*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Unregister-ScheduledTask -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

name: APT29 Stage 5 - Periodic DNS Beacon Pattern to Non-resolving Names (T1071.004)
blast_radius: Sends six DNS queries about two seconds apart, each for a unique run-tagged name under the reserved .invalid top-level domain, from the PowerShell process. Queries go to the host resolver and cannot resolve. This validates host DNS telemetry only; periodicity analytics and SIEM ingestion are not verified.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 22: DNS query events for the run-tagged names
DNS-Client Operational EID 3008 where that channel is enabled
DNS server log: queries for the .invalid names
detection: DNS analytics: periodic queries with high-entropy labels to one parent domain
Resolver policy: .invalid names should never leave the resolver
